The completed diagnostic requires the protected existing environment/model and the original eight-arm reproduction archive. No automatic rerun is authorized by these commands. Acquire fresh finite native Windows benchmark_quiet admission, verify project procedures and pins, prepare exact restoration, then use a broker-mediated finite launcher. Never reuse completed credentials. Preserve the product source and completed outputs; adapt output paths in a separate task scope and refreeze before a separately authorized reproduction.

CPU guard: `.venv/bin/python -B score_components/diagnostic/CPU.py` (266 passed, CUDA forbidden). The frozen diagnostic is `score_components/diagnostic/run.py current_profile`; it uses PYTHONHASHSEED=4109 and the unchanged 45-request trace. The existing directory deliberately refuses overwrite. The run calls the owned ASGI export endpoint after load completion; native worker collective RPC explicitly drains profiles, writes real snapshots, and runs ONE forced-min-pool-1 replay within the existing context. This is postload and does not feed policy. Diagnostic source differs only by the supplied profiling patch; all driver/runtime/JSON instrumentation is task-local and pinned in evidence/frozen.json.

Analysis only: `score_components/diagnostic/finish_analysis.py` and `write_report.py` consume retained files. No model, CUDA initialization, download, build or workload rerun is required. Full tensor corpus is results/current_profile/explicit-export/replay.pt; components, per-query recall, actual scheduler queues, source/runtime profiles and lossless logs are archived. Eight-arm archive is ../reproduction-tools.tar.gz with ../evidence/export-manifest.json. These summaries are inclusive wall/threadCPU/sampled CUDA ranges, not additive costs. Cold index initialization and large-pool crossover remain unresolved.
